ForestPlots.net Training Manual ForestPlots Team, University of Leeds 2026-10-19 Welcome Welcome to the ForestPlots.net Training Manual. This guide is designed to help new and existing users of ForestPlots.net — the global network for monitoring tropical forest plots — to get the most out of the platform. How to use this manual This manual is organised into chapters that follow a natural workflow, from creating an account through to downloading and analysing data. You can read it sequentially or jump to the chapter most relevant to your needs. The following is all soon to be created! New users should start with Chapters ?? and ??. Data contributors will find Chapters ?? and ?? most useful. Data users seeking to query or download data should head to Chapter ??. R users will find the RAINFOR / ForestPlots R package covered in Chapter ??. About ForestPlots.net ForestPlots.net is a pan-tropical network and database hosting long-term forest inventory data from permanent sample plots across the tropics. It supports research into forest dynamics, carbon stocks, and ecosystem responses to climate change.

Before you start This document is living and is being created currently for the benefit of all users. There already exists a ForestPlots user manual, but we hope that this document can accompany that to guide users through case examples to work with their data. It is extremely important that a member of the ForestPlots team first shows you how to work with the data before you attempt to do this on your own. In the meantime, your feedback is especially important so if you find that it is not meeting your needs, please inform a member of the ForestPlots team so that we can improve this document.

Query Checks What are the query checks? After you have completed the tree checks, it is important to run the query checks to look at the overall plot level dynamics. Before we look at the query library to perform some calculations, let’s verify some information about our plots. Verify important plot infromation 1. Read all plot notes Some valuable information may be hiding in the plot notes. Read the plot notes to ensure you have an entire picture of what may be happening in the plot before you view the outputs of the query library and freak out. 2. Create and define preferred plot views Sometimes we only want to look at a piece of a plot. For whatever reason this may be, you can create a plot view on ForestPlots to ensure that you are viewing the correct part of your plot. If you are unfamiliar with plot views, you can read about them here. It is important to know that when performing queries in the query library we should use the ‘Preferred Plot View’ = TRUE. 3. Check the plot area Has the plot area been defined correctly on the Details page of the plot and in the plot view? 4. Check census dates Census dates will directly impact the calculations we will shortly make. If the census dates are incorrect, you will get very weird values. Double check the census dates! 5. Click ‘refresh plot views’ The plot views need to be refreshed after you have modified POMs or data in the plot. Be sure to go to the Plot View and click the ‘refresh plot views’ button or your results will be weird. Run the query checks In the query checks stage, there are 4 main parts to verify: Basal area Above Ground Biomass (AGB) Above-Ground Wood Production (AGWP) Turnover We are running these queries to ensure that the plot dynamics fall within a normal range and follow the general trend of the plot. If the plot values fall outside the range or stray from the general trend, then this may mean that we missed something during the tree checks or that the tree checks did not pick something up. However, it is also possible that the outcomes are completely normal, and this is when on the ground knowledge is vital to inform us of these strange values. With this context, let’s begin. To run these queries, we will be using the query library. For each query, Click the bars tab on the left-side of the ForestPlots screen Choose the private tab Choose the necessary query: Basal area: click ‘Basal Area’, then ’Plot Basal Area by Census (m2 ha-1) AGB: click ‘Biomass’, then the appropriate allometric equation (we tend to use AGB Chave 2014 for moist forests) AGWP: click ‘Wood Productivity’, then the appropriate allometric equation (we tend to use AGWP Chave Moist (Ht Weibull, Regional) for moist forests) Turnover: click ‘Turnover’, then ‘Stem Dynamics by Interval’ Choose the necessary plots Save as Excel The typical range of outputs for each query can be found in the ForestPlots tracker in the tracker_headers tab with the associated green section (Q7 to Q10). If values that fall outside of these typical ranges are found, then confirm that the Automated POM Change Wizard was run, the Plot Views have been refreshed, and the Census Dates are correct. If all of these are verified, then we should look at the data more deeply. If this occurs, please contact your fellow ForestPlots team member to guide you through this process. We will work to add more information to this section shortly!

Liana data Collecting liana data To collect liana data for a new plot, you can use a liana fieldsheet. If you already have existing liana data, then generate a liana fieldsheet on ForestPlots from within your plot. See below!     Prepare data for upload Data must be in the exact correct format before being uploaded to ForestPlots. So first and foremost, ensure you have all the necessary columns and that they are spelled exactly how they are listed on the liana fieldsheet. To understand how to fill in each column, view the Definitions tab of the liana fieldsheet. If you still encounter issues, here is some information to help address some of the most common mistakes that people make: Tag No versus New Tag No column Tag No contains all of the tag numbers of the liana stems, but what is the purpose of the New Tag No column? The New Tag No column is used to update the tag numbers of stems in Forestplots. When uploading data, only the New Tag No column will be used, not Tag No. Whether you are uploading lianas for the first time or uploading an additional liana census, use the New Tag No column. When uploading lianas for the first time, there are no records of tag numbers so you must write all of the tag numbers in the New Tag No column. When uploading an additional liana census, there are existing tag numbers in the database. Therefore, you do not need to upload all of the tag numbers again. Instead, you only need to upload the tag numbers for new recruits (stems that have no records of a tag number) and stems that have had their tag number changed. Therefore, fill in the New Tag No column for all new recruits or when a liana’s tag number changes. There is no need to fill in the New Tag No column for a stem whose tag remains the same. Have you filled Most Affected Tree and Host trees columns correctly? The Most Affected Tree and Host trees column must contain the Tree ID of the tree you are referencing, not the Tag No.  Most people find this frustrating because the field sheet gives this value as the tag number and not the Tree ID. The reason for this is that as you can imagine the tag number is more helpful in the field than the Tree ID. But if the Tree ID is not given to you in the field sheet how do you find it? To get the Tree ID, you can go to the Vegetation tab of your plot, click Trees, and search the Tag No in this section and copy the Tree ID from here.     You can also download a Plot Dump and find the tree and Tree ID there. Fill in the flag3 and flag4 column for alive lianas! It is commonly forgotten to fill in the Flag3 and Flag4 columns (L.F3, L.F4, etc.). However, it is a requirement of ForestPlots to fill these in. As a quick summary, flag 3 describes how the measurement was taken and Flag 4 describes whether the value was modified. For most cases, you can fill in the Flag 3 and Flag 4 columns as 0. However, if the diameter was measured with something other than a tape measure or was retrospectively modified, then view the Flag options here and fill in the column with the correct code. Upload data To upload liana data, navigate to the Data Import section and click ‘Go’!     Hint: the green down arrow button next to “Import Liana Plot Data” contains the upload template you filled in earlier. The “Plot Census” button refers to the tree censuses that are stored in ForestPlots. Since lianas are typically collected at the same time as trees, choose the tree census that occurred simultaneously as the liana census that is being currently being uploaded. The button, “Copy participants from linked plot census?”, allows for all participants in the chosen Plot Census to be automatically copied to the liana census being uploaded. Click this button if all participants of the associated tree census should be associated with the liana census being uploaded.     Fill in the census dates and any comments that you need to be uploaded for this census. Select the file to be uploaded. If there is anything wrong with the data you are trying to upload, you will be told here. You can either fix the individual issues here or go back to the Excel file, fix the issues, and re-do the upload. Sign off data Once the data has been uploaded, we need to check that the data is okay. The first step is to run the ‘Liana Dynamics’ Query which will tell us whether the data is consistent or not: Click on the Query Library Icon on the left-hand side of the screen Select ‘Private’ Click on ‘Lianas’ in the empty box Select ‘Liana Dynamics’, click on the green arrow Click ‘next’ Filter for your plots, then add your plots by selecting the ‘add’ icon (You can add many at a time) Click ‘Next’ at the bottom of the page Select ‘Save to excel’ Open the Excel file and check the last column ‘Consistency Check’ where we expect all of the values of this column to be zero If 0, no inconsistencies were found in the liana data (move to sign off the data) If 1, extra values were found in the liana data (check the data for lianas recorded as alive after being recorded as dead) If -1, missing values were found in the liana data (check the data for lianas with missing information) Fix the inconsistencies in the liana data Extra values in the liana data If you find that the Consistency Check in the Lianas Dynamic Query has given you a number greater than 0, then it typically means that a liana was recorded as dead or not recorded. To check for this, you can either download a liana field sheet and manually look for these trees, or you can generate a list of the lianas that have an issue. To generate the list of lianas that have back to life lianas or missing lianas, follow these steps: Click on the Query Library Icon on the left-hand side of the screen Select ‘Private’ Click on ‘Lianas’ in the empty box Select ‘QC Lianas recorded as Alive after being recorded as Dead’ Select the necessary plot(s) Click ‘Next’ on the bottom of the page Select ‘Save to excel’ This excel file now has a list of the plots (column B), lianas (column E), and the census where the liana came back to life or was missed (column F and I). Missing values in the liana data If you find that the Consistency Check in the Lianas Dynamic Query has given you a number greater than 0, then it typically means that a liana was missed in the data. To check for this, you can either download a liana field sheet and manually look for these trees, or you can generate a list of the lianas that have an issue. To generate the list of lianas that have back to life lianas or missing lianas, follow these steps: Click on the Query Library Icon on the left-hand side of the screen Select ‘Private’ Click on ‘Lianas’ in the empty box Select ‘QC Lianas with missing censuses’ Select the highlighted plots Click ‘Next’ on the bottom of the page Select ‘Save to excel’ This Excel file now has the list of plots (column B) and the lianas (columns E and F) that have one or more censuses missing (Column C). Fix the issues on ForestPlots To fix the issues identified above, we recommend downloading a liana field sheet, viewing the errors there in its entirety, and modifying the errors there in a different color. To download the field sheet, Go to the plot and select ‘Data Export’ Click on ‘Generate Liana Field Sheet’ Open the excel file and check the values of flagged lianas To correctly modify the data, first check the values against the original field sheets or, when field sheets are not available, in the original data If values are missing, interpolate the diameter when necessary Once you have identified the errors, and recorded the changes you want to make, you can modify each liana one-by-one on the ForestPlots platform: Open the plot on the platform and go to ‘Vegetation’ Click on arrow in box to select ‘Lianas’ Search for the lianas using the Tag No or Tree ID column Correct the values manually by clicking the magnifying glass icon, then edit After all of the values have been modified, re-run the ‘Liana Dynamics’ Query and repeat these steps if necessary. No inconsistencies in the liana data When there are no inconsistencies in the liana data (aka Consistency Check = 0), we can sign off the the liana data! To sign off the liana data, Open the plot Click ‘Details’ on the plot menu Click ‘Edit’ in the top right Click on the ‘Forest Inventory’ section Fill in the information ‘Liana Sample’ with “Where the liana data is stored + the liana census you signed off + the date the liana census was signed off”, e.g. ForestPlots.net; Liana Census 3; QCJan2026 Even though the data has been signed off, it does not mean that people with access to this plot can see this liana census. To check if the liana data has been released to all members who have access to the plot, Navigate to the Plot page Click Censuses Choose Liana Censuses If the lock is red, this means only you can see the liana plot census. If the lock is green, this means everyone who has access to the plot can see the liana census. It is important to ensure everyone in your plot can see the liana census. To change the view rights of this census, Click the magnifying glass icon at the right of the census Click Edit And ensure “Is Released to My Plots” is set to TRUE All done! Top work! Now you have uploaded and signed off liana data to your plot. Congratulations!
